### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**2** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), getMetaItemLayered (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via getPublished (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/published; the bare tail of client method meta.getPublished, bound to GET /meta/:type/:name/published))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/published (route, bridged from symbol getMetaItemLayered — its route source's handler names it))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2cba2eb3f1f50ff1678dfa7b2925e37965b6f9c5` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c75a860e95ab6982e978dc92a2681d4ebb51e093` — the merge of head `c53513be600f1dec1a07824f133c73691f8c7214` into base `2cba2eb3f1f50ff1678dfa7b2925e37965b6f9c5`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c75a860e95ab6982e978dc92a2681d4ebb51e093 && git checkout c75a860e95ab6982e978dc92a2681d4ebb51e093
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2cba2eb3f1f50ff1678dfa7b2925e37965b6f9c5 c53513be600f1dec1a07824f133c73691f8c7214 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2cba2eb3f1f50ff1678dfa7b2925e37965b6f9c5 && git merge --no-ff c53513be600f1dec1a07824f133c73691f8c7214

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2cba2eb3f1f50ff1678dfa7b2925e37965b6f9c5
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2cba2eb3f1f50ff1678dfa7b2925e37965b6f9c5` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `c53513be600f1dec1a07824f133c73691f8c7214`
Local-runs: none

Reviewed at 2026-11-02T00:21Z against the merge-base `1920e4801ab96426bb624470bceedef41066ad16` (PR #28828's squash) for PR #28845 (card #28830, `Fixes #28830`), one commit, four files: `.changeset/28830-layered-read-pair-added-member.md`, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (+34/-8), `packages/objectql/src/protocol-bundle-member-base-address.test.ts` (+69), `packages/qa/dogfood/test/email-template-dependent-unshipped-locale-read.dogfood.test.ts` (+35/-1). Face: `record-recognisers --paths` decides no face on the four paths (no published schema, no governed rule text) and defers to the committed changeset's `Clause-②: yes (widening)` line, which is the declaration face: `TIER_DEFAULT`. Read-only: the diff, the card, the claim, the os-dev-report, the gate record, the PR body, the head's check-runs, PR #28828's two review records, ADR-0146 D8 (on `origin/main`), and the cited code at the head (`readMetaItem`, `getMetaItemLayered`, `findServedOverlayRow` / `servedOverlayRowCandidates`, `pairOfAddedMember`, `registryMemberServedAt`, `bundleMemberDiscriminator`, `packagelessReadAddress` / `packagelessContentPackage` / `packagelessAddress`, `readVersionToken` / `storedHeadAt`, `servedLockState`, the REST `/layers` route and `createMetaLayeredAnswer`). Nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**1. Semantics of the layered read, by case (bundle types only; `email_template` is the one `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` entry today).** Judged on the head's code. In `getMetaItemLayered`, `contentPackageId` is `request.packageId` or `packagelessReadAddress`, which at this head is `packagelessContentPackage(packagelessAddress(...), shippedArtifactsOf(...))`: the one code package that ships the name (BASE) whether the stored rows at the member are bound to PAIR, to DEPENDENT or to both (#28238, D8 item 1). So the package-less read and the base-named read take the same path below, and the by-name read's `contentPackageId` is derived the same way (`readMetaItem`, #28238), so the two reads agree by construction.

- **Pair's own added member on the base's address (`?package=BASE` or no package).** The served-row resolution (`findServedOverlayRow`, `servedOverride`, candidates: the base's declared override, the base's own row, the package-less row) finds nothing at `fr-FR`; the new branch runs (`!served`, `wantedMember` = `fr-FR`, `contentPackageId` = BASE): `findPairAddedMemberRow` asks `pairOfAddedMember` (BASE ships the name, does not ship `fr-FR`, `BASE.custom` is its pair) and reads `findServedOverlayRow({ packageId: PAIR, member })`: the pair's row. `overlay` is that row, `overlayScope: 'env'`, `code` stays as resolved (`null`: the service copy is another member, the artifact lookup at `fr-FR` misses, the registry's bare slot holds a tenant-authored hydrated row and `runtimeOnly` drops it), `effective` is the overlay (not orphaned, not a declining type). Before the diff all three were `null`, which `createMetaLayeredAnswer` refuses as `absent` and the door writes as `404`. **404 → the pair's layer. Correct, as ordered.**
- **A dependent's added member on the base's address.** Same path to the new branch; `pairOfAddedMember` names only `BASE.custom`, `findServedOverlayRow` is asked for the pair's row and there is none; `served` stays `undefined`; `overlay` `null`, `code` `null`; the view-container expansion does not apply; the orphan block needs `code !== null` and is skipped. All three `null` → `404`. **Unchanged.** Under `?package=DEPENDENT`, `contentPackageId` = DEPENDENT and the first resolution serves its own row; the new branch is not reached (and `pairOfAddedMember(..., DEPENDENT, ...)` would answer `undefined`: it ships no bundle of the name). **Unchanged, served under its own package.**
- **Pair and dependent both at `fr-FR`.** The first resolution on the base's address still finds nothing (a dependent's row is never a candidate of BASE's address: `servedOverlayRowCandidates` with a package is that package's row then the package-less row). The new branch names PAIR explicitly, so the dependent's row is never read. The package-less read resolves `contentPackageId` to BASE here too (`packagelessAddress` sees two bindings → `null`; `packagelessContentPackage` with one shipper → BASE). **The pair's. Correct**, and deterministic regardless of hydration order (the registry's bare slot is not consulted on this path).
- **The base's own member (`en-US`).** When no row is stored, `served` is `undefined` and the new branch asks `pairOfAddedMember(..., 'en-US')`: BASE ships that member → `undefined` → no read. `code` the base's artifact, `overlay: null`. **Unchanged.**
- **A declared override (`en-US` in the pair with `overrides.package = BASE`).** The first resolution's `servedOverride` candidate serves it; `served` is set, the new branch is skipped. `code` the base's, `overlay` the override, `effective` the override. **Unchanged.** The dogfood control also pins that `fr-FR` on the base stays `404` when only the override is stored.
- **`?package=PAIR`.** `contentPackageId` = PAIR; the first resolution serves the pair's own row at `fr-FR`. **Unchanged.**
- **Non-bundle types.** `bundleMemberDiscriminator` returns `undefined` for a type with no `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` entry, so `wantedMember !== undefined` is false and the branch never runs; the `const served` → `let served` typing is a no-op. **Byte-identical behaviour by construction**; the objectql control pins a `view` on the base (`code` the base's columns, `overlay: null`).
- **`/published` and the other readers of `getMetaItemLayered`** (`meta-item-history-routes.ts`, runtime `meta.ts`): the `/published` door reads the layered `overlay` for a name on the package-less address; for a pair-added member it now serves the pair's row where it answered the MetadataService's `getPublished` fallback or absence before. That is the same widening on the same seam, consistent with D8 ("the layered read's `effective` and the plain read serve one row"). Not pinned by the tests; noted, not a defect.

**2. One seam, PR #28828's predicate.** Exactly one new behavioural branch in `getMetaItemLayered`. The new private `findPairAddedMemberRow` is the #28802 branch of `readMetaItem` lifted verbatim: `pairOfAddedMember` (→ `shipsBundleName`, `shippedArtifactsOf(..., member)`, `customizationPackageId`) then `findServedOverlayRow({ packageId: pair, state: 'active', ...memberOption(member) }, activeRows)`, `?.row`. The by-name refactor is behaviour-preserving: before, `record` was reassigned only when `pairOfAddition !== undefined` and was otherwise already falsy (`served?.row` of an `undefined` `served`); after, it is assigned the helper's result, which is `undefined` in exactly those cases and the same `?.row` otherwise; `storedRowServed` (`record !== undefined && record !== null`) and every later read of `record` see identical values; `activeRows` is still forwarded. The bundle-type gate is the same table on both reads (`bundleMemberDiscriminator` → `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS`; no `'email_template'` literal in the diff). **One seam, one predicate, no second spelling. Correct.** The layered call passes no `activeRows`, so the helper reads the store once more there; the by-name read keeps its pre-read rows. Fine.

**3. Lock, flags, stamp.** `overlayLockLayerAt` and `artifactLockLayerAt` are asked at `request.packageId` as before, so the lock is unchanged. `servedLockState`'s last argument (`overlay !== null && !orphaned`) is now true for a pair-added member on the base's address; per its docblock that boolean feeds only the origin-gated removal verdict, and the by-name read has reported the same (`storedRowServed` true through its 1b branch) since PR #28828, so the two reads agree. `overlayRow` is set from the pair's row; `declinesStoredRow` reads it for `flow` and code-defined `datasource` names only, neither a bundle type. The layered read reports layers, not a `_packageId` stamp of its own; `overlay` is the row as stored. **Consistent.**

**4. Evidence.**
- Red first: dogfood on main `1920e480` 2 failed / 10 passed (the pair's layered case and the pair-beside-dependent case), 12/12 at the head under the lock. The new objectql `[#28830]` describe is reported green at the head (10/10 for the file) with no run on main; its red is the ablation leg (below). Consistent with the diff's one behaviour change.
- Ablation, the seam only: `if (row) served = { row };` → `void row;` via `ablation-replace.mjs`, `dist/` preflight `--absent`, restore blob verified: unit 2 red / 8 green, dogfood 2 red / 10 green, the pair-added cases alone; dependent cases and every control green. As reported; not re-run here. The by-name refactor has no ablation leg; it is judged above by reading and by the by-name suites staying green (metadata-protocol 297 files / 22080 tests, objectql 521 files / 10008 tests at the head, as reported). **Accepted.**
- Controls present: the base's `en-US` layers on every read; the pair's declared `en-US` override; `fr-FR` on the base `404` with only that override stored; `?package=PAIR` unchanged; a dependent's `fr-FR` `404` on the base and package-less reads and served under the dependent; a non-bundle `view` on the base. The order's control list is covered.
- Gates: the gate record lists 66 families, all exit 0 (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` re-run after a prerequisite build). Check-runs on the head at read time: 30 success, 13 skipped, 5 in progress, 0 failures (`Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, Build Core, ESLint and every Type Check family success; Test Core shards 1, 3, 5, 6 and 7 in progress). The dogfood shards are skipped on the PR run; the flipped dogfood file first runs in CI in the merge group.
- Overlap: `origin/main` has moved one `protocol.ts` commit past the merge-base (PR #28811, object extensions; hunks at the overlay merge and the package domains, none in `readMetaItem`, `getMetaItemLayered` or the #28802 helpers); `git merge-tree` of the head against current `origin/main` writes a clean tree. Open PRs on `packages/metadata-protocol/src/`: #28731 (`protocol.ts` hunks near the by-id OCC comparison, lines 3201 / 14446 / 14665 / 14774), #28843 (`protocol.ts` one hunk near 14733), #28764 (`metadata-redaction.ts`). None touches the three regions this diff moves (11518, 12218, 17408). #28838 is merged (one test file). Seat 1's #28831 (the per-package layer's stamp) has no PR and works the list read's per-package layer, not this path.

### ② Semver level

- **`Clause-②: yes (widening)` — correct.** A public read, `GET /meta/email_template/NAME/layers?member=LOCALE` naming the base or no package, answered `404` for a pair-added member and now answers `200` with the pair's layer (and `/published` follows). No address lost an answer: every other case above is unchanged, so there is no narrowing arm to declare. Title carries no `!`.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — correct.** AGENTS.md rule 3 defines the line as the change to what a metadata author can write. Nothing authorable is added, refused or tightened, and no meaning or default changes: what a pair-added locale means on the base's address was decided by PR #28828 (`semantic` there); this read reports it. `none` ⇒ `patch` on every introduced entry.
- **Changeset `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: patch` — correct.** `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`'s level axis: `none` grades every entry `patch`, with no authorable-surface baseline moved; the gate record has it exit 0 and `Check Changeset` concluded success on the head. Both declaration lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body. No `Skills-docs:` line is owed (`none` kind, no `(narrowing)` arm). Full dogfood battery not owed (`(widening)` arm, no `!`).

### ③ Boundary flags

Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no relay login to name.

- **Open question (the `version` token) — answer A, leave as is; a note, not a card.** Measured by the dev on main: the base-named by-name read of a pair-added `fr-FR` answers `version: null`; the package-less and pair-named reads answer the pair row's token. This is the documented contract of `version`, not a defect: `readVersionToken`'s docblock says the token is "the address of the SAVE, not of the served content", that "a token of a row the save would not overwrite would be refused by that save every time, so such a read serves `null` rather than the served row's token", and that a `null` says a save at that address is a create. Naming the base, `storedHeadAt(..., BASE, 'fr-FR')` finds no row; naming none, `packagelessAddress` binds to the one package's row at the member (PAIR), which is the row a package-less save would overwrite, so its token is served. Answering the pair's token on the base-named read would hand out a pin the save door naming the base refuses, which is the OCC chain's one rule. The layered read carries no `version` field, so this PR neither touches nor could touch it. No door edits a pair-added member through the base's address today; the by-name read's `editable`/`version: null` pair on that address is the dormant shape to watch. Record the measurement on the card at close; file a card only if a client is measured re-pinning a save from the base-named read (e.g. an editor that opens a bundle member through `?package=BASE` and saves there), and that card is the save door's routing, not this read's.
- **Should-fix (seat, prose face, not this review's): docs.** The Docs Drift Check names `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx` via `getMetaItemLayered`; the open #28829 (the skills/docs card from PR #28828, carried by PR #28814) teaches the pair-added-locale behaviour on those pages. One line there that the layered read now agrees would close the D8 story in the docs; no line is owed on this PR.
- **Should-fix (test, optional):** the package-less layered read in the pair-beside-dependent case is asserted on neither file (both assert the base-named read only). Judged correct above by the shared `packagelessContentPackage` derivation; one expectation on `layersOf(protocol, TYPE, NAME, 'fr-FR')` in that unit case would pin it.
- **Note:** the PR body's "before" column says `404` for the package-less layered read of a pair-added member; that reading is consistent with the code (the package-less `contentPackageId` resolved to BASE before the diff too) though the dogfood's red run stopped at the base-named assertion, so the package-less `404` on main is derived, not measured.
- Dormant notes carried from PR #28828's records (`previewDrafts` of a pair-added member; the package-unbound row's ordering at an unshipped member) stand and are untouched here.
- **Landing precheck ②:** CI on the head is not complete at review time (5 Test Core shards in progress, 0 failures); the flipped dogfood file first runs in the merge group. The record stands for this head only. The branch is one commit on the merge-base; `main` has moved by PR #28811 with no textual or semantic overlap.
